items.q: A survey line of 50 m has a whole circle bearing of 45 degrees. Find its latitude.
items.s: Latitude = L cos(bearing) = 50 × cos 45 = 35.36 m.

items.s: Misclosure = square root of (0.9 squared + 1.6 squared) = 1.84 m.

items.q: Two stations differ by 10 m easting and 30 m northing. Find the whole circle bearing of the line joining them, both differences being positive.
items.s: tan(bearing) = departure ÷ latitude = 10 ÷ 30, so the bearing is 18.43 degrees.

items.q: The coordinates of two points differ by 40 m in easting and 40 m in northing. Find the distance between them.
items.s: Distance = square root of (40 squared + 40 squared) = 56.57 m.

items.q: The height of collimation is 105.2 m and the foresight staff reading is 2.4 m. Find the reduced level of the point sighted.
items.s: Reduced level = height of instrument − foresight = 105.2 − 2.4 = 102.8 m.

items.q: A backsight of 2.2 m is taken to a bench mark of reduced level 98.6 m. Find the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 98.6 + 2.2 = 100.8 m.

items.q: The staff reading at one station is 2 m and at the next is 1.2 m. Taking the first reading minus the second, find the rise or fall.
items.s: Difference = 2 − 1.2 = 0.8 m; a positive result is a rise.

items.q: The angles of a closed traverse of 4 sides add up to 360.05 degrees, while the theoretical sum is 360 degrees. Find the angular misclosure.
items.s: Misclosure = observed sum − theoretical sum = 360.05 − 360 = 0.05 degrees.

items.q: A traverse of 8 angles closes with a misclosure of 0.04 degrees. Find the correction to be applied to each angle, the error being shared equally.
items.s: Correction per angle = misclosure ÷ number of angles = 0.04 ÷ 8 = 0.005 degrees.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of reducing levels through the height of the line of sight”?
o: horizontal equivalent
contour interval
foresight
height of collimation method
items.s: height of collimation method is the method of reducing levels through the height of the line of sight.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines transit theodolite?
o: the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
the method of reducing levels by comparing successive staff readings
a theodolite whose telescope can be turned completely over
a range of wavelengths recorded as one channel
items.s: transit theodolite: a theodolite whose telescope can be turned completely over. The other options describe spectral band, attribute data, rise and fall.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines horizontal equivalent?
o: the scale stated as the ratio of map distance to ground distance
the vertical distance between successive contours
the ground distance between successive contours
the strip of ground covered as the sensor moves forward
items.s: horizontal equivalent: the ground distance between successive contours. The other options describe contour interval, representative fraction, satellite swath.

items.q: The statement “a traverse that begins and ends at known points” describes which of the following?
o: traverse
check line
linear misclosure
closed traverse
items.s: closed traverse is a traverse that begins and ends at known points.

items.q: Which of the following best describes precision of a survey?
o: the first sight taken to a point of known level
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
the closeness of repeated measurements to one another
a sensor that sends out its own signal and records the return
items.s: precision of a survey: the closeness of repeated measurements to one another. The other options describe backsight, active sensor, face right observation.

items.q: Which term is described by “a question answered by selecting features according to their position”?
o: layer in a GIS
spatial query
georeferencing
overlay analysis
items.s: spatial query is a question answered by selecting features according to their position.

items.q: leg of a traverse may be defined as
o: the volume of water a reservoir can hold
the method of reducing levels through the height of the line of sight
one measured line between two stations
a measure of the scatter of repeated observations
items.s: leg of a traverse: one measured line between two stations. The other options describe probable error, capacity of a reservoir, height of collimation method.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines end area.
o: the computation of area from the coordinates of the boundary points
the direction of a line measured clockwise from a stated reference meridian
the distance by which a closed traverse fails to return to its start
the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork
items.s: end area: the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork. The other options describe azimuth, coordinate method of area, closing error.

items.q: The statement “the reduced level of the line of sight of a level” describes which of the following?
o: spot level
bench mark
height of instrument
height of collimation method
items.s: height of instrument is the reduced level of the line of sight of a level.

items.q: Which term is described by “the difference between an observed value and its adjusted value”?
o: bowditch rule
residual
closing on a known point
transit rule
items.s: residual is the difference between an observed value and its adjusted value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes accuracy of a survey?
o: the ground distance between successive contours
the reduced level of a single point on the ground
the sight taken to the point whose level is required
the closeness of a result to its true value
items.s: accuracy of a survey: the closeness of a result to its true value. The other options describe horizontal equivalent, spot level, foresight.

items.q: angular misclosure may be defined as
o: the direction of a line measured clockwise from north
the amount by which the sum of observed angles differs from the theoretical sum
the volume computed using end areas and a mid section
the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
items.s: angular misclosure: the amount by which the sum of observed angles differs from the theoretical sum. The other options describe prismoidal rule, bearing, attribute data.

items.q: angle of depression may be defined as
o: the reduced level of a single point on the ground
the length of the closing error of a traverse
the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal
the difference between an observed value and its adjusted value
items.s: angle of depression: the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal. The other options describe linear misclosure, spot level, residual.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines representative fraction.
o: the method of reducing levels through the height of the line of sight
the scale stated as the ratio of map distance to ground distance
a bearing stated from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
the reduced level of the line of sight of a level
items.s: representative fraction: the scale stated as the ratio of map distance to ground distance. The other options describe height of instrument, whole circle bearing, height of collimation method.

items.q: The statement “the direction of a line measured clockwise from a stated reference meridian” describes which of the following?
o: azimuth
traverse station
reduced bearing
departure of a line
items.s: azimuth is the direction of a line measured clockwise from a stated reference meridian.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines transit rule.
o: the adjustment that minimises the sum of squares of the corrections
the reduced level of the line of sight of a level
the adjustment that shares the error in proportion to the latitudes and departures
the volume computed using end areas and a mid section
items.s: transit rule: the adjustment that shares the error in proportion to the latitudes and departures. The other options describe prismoidal rule, least squares adjustment, height of instrument.

items.q: Which of the following best describes planimeter?
o: the method of reducing levels through the height of the line of sight
the reduced level of a single point on the ground
a set of mapped features of one kind held together in a system
the instrument that measures the area of a figure traced by hand
items.s: planimeter: the instrument that measures the area of a figure traced by hand. The other options describe spot level, layer in a GIS, height of collimation method.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines prismoidal rule?
o: a theodolite whose telescope can be turned completely over
the amount by which the sum of observed angles differs from the theoretical sum
the vertical distance between successive contours
the volume computed using end areas and a mid section
items.s: prismoidal rule: the volume computed using end areas and a mid section. The other options describe angular misclosure, contour interval, transit theodolite.

items.q: Which term is described by “the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read”?
o: permanent adjustment
temporary adjustment
face left observation
horizontal circle
items.s: horizontal circle is the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read.

items.q: Which term is described by “the tying of an image or map to real world coordinates”?
o: resolution of a raster
spatial query
vector data
georeferencing
items.s: georeferencing is the tying of an image or map to real world coordinates.

items.q: Which term is described by “the vertical distance between successive contours”?
o: interpolation of contours
height of collimation method
reduced level
contour interval
items.s: contour interval is the vertical distance between successive contours.

o: geographic information system
attribute data
prismoidal rule
layer in a GIS
items.s: Every other option belongs to Geographic information systems. “prismoidal rule” belongs to Area and volume, not Geographic information systems.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of reducing levels by comparing successive staff readings”?
o: foresight
spot level
rise and fall
interpolation of contours
items.s: rise and fall is the method of reducing levels by comparing successive staff readings.

items.q: Which of the following best describes telescope bubble?
o: the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
the northward or southward component of a survey line
the level bubble used to set the line of sight horizontal
the scale stated as the ratio of map distance to ground distance
items.s: telescope bubble: the level bubble used to set the line of sight horizontal. The other options describe vertical circle, latitude of a line, representative fraction.

items.q: The statement “the adjustment that shares the error in proportion to the latitudes and departures” describes which of the following?
o: angular misclosure
transit rule
accuracy of a survey
bowditch rule
items.s: transit rule is the adjustment that shares the error in proportion to the latitudes and departures.

items.q: The statement “a traverse that does not return to its starting point” describes which of the following?
o: azimuth
open traverse
closed traverse
whole circle bearing
items.s: open traverse is a traverse that does not return to its starting point.

items.q: The statement “the volume of water a reservoir can hold” describes which of the following?
o: trapezoidal rule
representative fraction
traverse area
capacity of a reservoir
items.s: capacity of a reservoir is the volume of water a reservoir can hold.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines overlay analysis?
o: the combining of two map layers to produce a new layer
one cell of a raster image
the gathering of information about the earth without touching it
a fixed point of known elevation from which levels are taken
items.s: overlay analysis: the combining of two map layers to produce a new layer. The other options describe remote sensing, bench mark, pixel.

items.q: Which of the following best describes vector data?
o: the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork
the vertical angle measured upward from the horizontal
spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons
the northward or southward component of a survey line
items.s: vector data: spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons. The other options describe end area, angle of elevation, latitude of a line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spot level?
o: the vertical angle measured upward from the horizontal
the line passing through the optical centre of the telescope
the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
the reduced level of a single point on the ground
items.s: spot level: the reduced level of a single point on the ground. The other options describe angle of elevation, line of collimation, traverse area.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines ground truth?
o: the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
the ground distance between successive contours
the closeness of repeated measurements to one another
information gathered on the ground to check what a sensor records
items.s: ground truth: information gathered on the ground to check what a sensor records. The other options describe traverse area, horizontal equivalent, precision of a survey.

items.q: Which of the following best describes whole circle bearing?
o: the volume computed by taking each pair of sections as a trapezium
a bearing stated from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal
the vertical angle measured upward from the horizontal
items.s: whole circle bearing: a bearing stated from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees. The other options describe angle of depression, trapezoidal rule, angle of elevation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes layer in a GIS?
o: the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read
the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork
a set of mapped features of one kind held together in a system
the computation of area from the coordinates of the boundary points
items.s: layer in a GIS: a set of mapped features of one kind held together in a system. The other options describe horizontal circle, coordinate method of area, end area.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines remote sensing?
o: the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
a fixed point of known elevation from which levels are taken
the distance by which a closed traverse fails to return to its start
the gathering of information about the earth without touching it
items.s: remote sensing: the gathering of information about the earth without touching it. The other options describe bench mark, closing error, vertical circle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes ground truth?
o: a line on a map joining points of equal elevation
the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork
the instrument that measures horizontal and vertical angles precisely
information gathered on the ground to check what a sensor records
items.s: ground truth: information gathered on the ground to check what a sensor records. The other options describe end area, contour, theodolite.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines foresight.
o: the adjustment that minimises the sum of squares of the corrections
the sight taken to the point whose level is required
one cell of a raster image
a bearing stated from north or south toward east or west, not exceeding ninety degrees
items.s: foresight: the sight taken to the point whose level is required. The other options describe least squares adjustment, pixel, reduced bearing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines raster data.
o: the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
spatial data held as a grid of cells each carrying a value
a series of connected survey lines whose lengths and directions are measured
the computation of area from the coordinates of the boundary points
items.s: raster data: spatial data held as a grid of cells each carrying a value. The other options describe traverse area, coordinate method of area, traverse.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines reduced level.
o: the direction of a line measured clockwise from north
the elevation of a point above a stated datum
a series of connected survey lines whose lengths and directions are measured
the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
items.s: reduced level: the elevation of a point above a stated datum. The other options describe traverse area, traverse, bearing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes traverse area?
o: spatial data held as a grid of cells each carrying a value
a point at which the instrument is set up and angles are observed
a question answered by selecting features according to their position
the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
items.s: traverse area: the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates. The other options describe spatial query, traverse station, raster data.

items.q: spatial query may be defined as
o: the gathering of information about the earth without touching it
a question answered by selecting features according to their position
the tying of an image or map to real world coordinates
the adjustment that minimises the sum of squares of the corrections
items.s: spatial query: a question answered by selecting features according to their position. The other options describe georeferencing, least squares adjustment, remote sensing.

items.q: Which term is described by “the distribution of misclosure among the measured values”?
o: transit rule
adjustment of a traverse
accuracy of a survey
probable error
items.s: adjustment of a traverse is the distribution of misclosure among the measured values.

items.q: attribute data may be defined as
o: the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
ending a traverse at a point whose coordinates are already known
spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
items.s: attribute data: the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature. The other options describe vector data, face right observation, closing on a known point.

items.q: The statement “a sensor that records natural radiation reflected or emitted by the earth” describes which of the following?
o: ground truth
passive sensor
spatial resolution of an image
satellite swath
items.s: passive sensor is a sensor that records natural radiation reflected or emitted by the earth.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines face left observation?
o: the volume computed using end areas and a mid section
an angle read with the vertical circle on the left of the observer
the volume computed by taking each pair of sections as a trapezium
the direction of a line measured clockwise from north

items.q: check line may be defined as
o: an additional measurement taken to test the traverse
the direction of a line measured clockwise from north
the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read
the closeness of repeated measurements to one another

items.q: The statement “spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons” describes which of the following?
o: vector data
pixel
georeferencing
raster data
items.s: vector data is spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons.

items.q: The statement “the difference between an observed value and its adjusted value” describes which of the following?
o: probable error
transit rule
residual
precision of a survey
items.s: residual is the difference between an observed value and its adjusted value.

items.q: Which term is described by “the smallest ground detail that can be distinguished”?
o: spatial resolution of an image
multispectral image
passive sensor
reflectance
items.s: spatial resolution of an image is the smallest ground detail that can be distinguished.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines least squares adjustment?

the distribution of misclosure among the measured values
the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
the adjustment that minimises the sum of squares of the corrections
items.s: least squares adjustment: the adjustment that minimises the sum of squares of the corrections. The other options describe adjustment of a traverse, height of collimation method, attribute data.

items.q: The statement “a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data” describes which of the following?
o: resolution of a raster
geographic information system
vector data
layer in a GIS
items.s: geographic information system is a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data.

items.q: resolution of a raster may be defined as
o: the correction of the fixed relations between the parts of the instrument
the ground size represented by one cell of the data
the reduced level of a single point on the ground
the method of reducing levels by comparing successive staff readings
items.s: resolution of a raster: the ground size represented by one cell of the data. The other options describe spot level, rise and fall, permanent adjustment.

the combining of two map layers to produce a new layer
a question answered by selecting features according to their position
one cell of a raster image
items.s: pixel: one cell of a raster image. The other options describe overlay analysis, georeferencing, spatial query.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines backsight.
o: the first sight taken to a point of known level
the elevation of a point above a stated datum
the reduced level of a single point on the ground
the vertical distance between successive contours
items.s: backsight: the first sight taken to a point of known level. The other options describe reduced level, spot level, contour interval.

items.q: angle of depression is best described as
o: the line passing through the optical centre of the telescope
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal
the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
items.s: angle of depression: the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal. The other options describe line of collimation, vertical circle, face right observation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes bowditch rule?
o: the closeness of a result to its true value
a measure of the scatter of repeated observations
the distribution of misclosure among the measured values
the adjustment that shares the closing error in proportion to the length of each leg
items.s: bowditch rule: the adjustment that shares the closing error in proportion to the length of each leg. The other options describe accuracy of a survey, probable error, adjustment of a traverse.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the gathering of information about the earth without touching it”
o: passive sensor
remote sensing
multispectral image
spectral band
items.s: remote sensing is the gathering of information about the earth without touching it.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines traverse area.
o: the volume computed by taking each pair of sections as a trapezium
the shape and area of a cutting or embankment measured across the line
the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
the cross sectional area at one end of a length of earthwork
items.s: traverse area: the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates. The other options describe end area, trapezoidal rule, cross section.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines horizontal circle?
o: the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read
the vertical angle measured upward from the horizontal
the level bubble used to set the line of sight horizontal
the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
items.s: horizontal circle: the graduated circle from which horizontal angles are read. The other options describe vertical circle, angle of elevation, telescope bubble.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines vector data?
o: the combining of two map layers to produce a new layer
a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
a question answered by selecting features according to their position
spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons
items.s: vector data: spatial data represented as points, lines and polygons. The other options describe geographic information system, spatial query, overlay analysis.

items.q: departure of a line may be defined as
o: a series of connected survey lines whose lengths and directions are measured
the northward or southward component of a survey line
the eastward or westward component of a survey line
a bearing stated from north or south toward east or west, not exceeding ninety degrees
items.s: departure of a line: the eastward or westward component of a survey line. The other options describe latitude of a line, traverse, reduced bearing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines remote sensing.
o: a range of wavelengths recorded as one channel
information gathered on the ground to check what a sensor records
the gathering of information about the earth without touching it
a sensor that sends out its own signal and records the return
items.s: remote sensing: the gathering of information about the earth without touching it. The other options describe ground truth, spectral band, active sensor.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines geographic information system.
o: the ground size represented by one cell of the data
a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
a set of mapped features of one kind held together in a system
the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
items.s: geographic information system: a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data. The other options describe resolution of a raster, attribute data, layer in a GIS.

items.q: vertical circle may be defined as
o: the vertical angle measured upward from the horizontal
the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
the correction of the fixed relations between the parts of the instrument
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
items.s: vertical circle: the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read. The other options describe permanent adjustment, angle of elevation, face right observation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes attribute data?
o: one cell of a raster image
the ground size represented by one cell of the data
the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature
a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
items.s: attribute data: the descriptive information attached to a mapped feature. The other options describe pixel, geographic information system, resolution of a raster.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Traverse surveys?
o: satellite swath
open traverse
traverse
closed traverse
items.s: Every other option belongs to Traverse surveys. “satellite swath” belongs to Remote sensing, not Traverse surveys.

items.q: face right observation may be defined as
o: the vertical angle measured downward from the horizontal
the line passing through the optical centre of the telescope
a theodolite whose telescope can be turned completely over
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
items.s: face right observation: an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer. The other options describe angle of depression, transit theodolite, line of collimation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ground size represented by one cell of the data”?
o: attribute data
spatial query
resolution of a raster
layer in a GIS
items.s: resolution of a raster is the ground size represented by one cell of the data.

items.q: capacity of a reservoir may be defined as
o: the volume computed using end areas and a mid section
the instrument that measures the area of a figure traced by hand
the ratio between a distance on the map and the distance on the ground
the volume of water a reservoir can hold

items.q: Which of the following best describes face right observation?
o: the correction of the fixed relations between the parts of the instrument
an angle read with the vertical circle on the right of the observer
the level bubble used to set the line of sight horizontal
a theodolite whose telescope can be turned completely over

least squares adjustment
transit rule
adjustment of a traverse

the ground distance between successive contours
a fixed point of known elevation from which levels are taken
the reduced level of the line of sight of a level

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines rise and fall.

the method of reducing levels by comparing successive staff readings
the sight taken to the point whose level is required
the vertical distance between successive contours

items.q: Which term is described by “an additional measurement taken to test the traverse”?

linear misclosure
leg of a traverse
latitude of a line

items.q: Which statement correctly defines temporary adjustment?

the line passing through the optical centre of the telescope
the setting up of the instrument over a station and levelling it
the level bubble used to set the line of sight horizontal

items.q: Which term is described by “the volume computed using end areas and a mid section”?

capacity of a reservoir
representative fraction
prismoidal rule

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the smallest ground detail that can be distinguished”

multispectral image
active sensor
spectral band
items.s: spatial resolution of an image is the smallest ground detail that can be distinguished.

items.q: Which of the following best describes trapezoidal rule?

the area enclosed by a closed traverse, computed from its coordinates
the volume computed by taking each pair of sections as a trapezium
the volume computed using end areas and a mid section

the ground distance between successive contours

the gathering of information about the earth without touching it

remote sensing
reflectance
active sensor

the length of the closing error of a traverse

angular misclosure

probable error

the computation of area from the coordinates of the boundary points

the tying of an image or map to real world coordinates
a system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data

a series of connected survey lines whose lengths and directions are measured

a traverse that does not return to its starting point

the line passing through the optical centre of the telescope
the graduated circle from which vertical angles are read
an angle read with the vertical circle on the left of the observer

the instrument that measures horizontal and vertical angles precisely

items.q: Two points 20 m apart have reduced levels of 120 m and 125 m. Find the distance from the first point to the position of the 122 m contour.
Two cross sections 20 m apart have areas of 6 and 6 square metres. Find the volume by the trapezoidal rule.
items.s: Volume = length × (A1 + A2) ÷ 2 = 20 × (6 + 6) ÷ 2 = 120 cubic metres.

items.q: Two end sections 30 m apart have areas of 4 and 8 square metres and the mid section has an area of 9 square metres. Find the volume by the prismoidal rule.
items.s: Volume = L × (A1 + 4Am + A2) ÷ 6 = 30 × (4 + 4 × 9 + 8) ÷ 6 = 240 cubic metres.

items.q: A closed traverse has a total departure error of 0.3 m and a total latitude error of 0.4 m. Find the linear misclosure.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (0.3 squared + 0.4 squared) = 0.5 m.

items.q: The staff reading at one station is 2.4 m and at the next is 3.1 m. Taking the first reading minus the second, find the rise or fall.
items.s: Difference = 2.4 − 3.1 = -0.7 m; a positive result is a rise.

items.q: A raster covers 10000 square metres with a cell size of 1 m. Find the number of pixels.

items.s: tan(bearing) = departure ÷ latitude = 30 ÷ 40, so the bearing is 36.87 degrees.
